founderAuthorization.rule: Founder rule 2026-09-29: A blocked/review-pending package blocks ONLY its own dependency lane; implement the next independent eligible package in an isolated branch, validate, checkpoint, commit, prepare the frozen review bundle, mark it REVIEW_PENDING if Codex is unavailable, and continue; never modify a pending package's branch, bundle, clone, evidence or cycle state.
founderAuthorization.constraint: Tests and non-protected documentation only; no protected file, no pending package scope, no merge.

rationale: The PowerShell installer scripts only run at install time; the first Phase0 attempt showed install-time-only defects are expensive. This package checks every script with the real PowerShell 5.1 parser and safety rules and cross-checks the two install-time artifact verifiers.

F-T4-001.observed: The PowerShell verifier checks listed entries, hashes, reparse points and lockfile membership but not unlisted extra files; the Node verifier rejects them. install.ps1 runs the PowerShell verifier, then the optional install-prereqs.ps1 (-InstallPrereqs), then the Node verifier, all before bootstrap.
F-T4-001.impact: low: only listed and hash-verified scripts run before the Node verifier; an unlisted file is caught before bootstrap
F-T4-001.disposition: FOUNDER_DECISION_PENDING (protected file) as queue item V6-PKG-L2-PS-VERIFIER-UNLISTED-FILES

F-T4-REVIEW-001.observed: the web-request rule used src.includes on the whole file, so one guarded request satisfied the rule for every other request in an allowlisted script.
F-T4-REVIEW-001.fix: webRequestViolations checks every Invoke-WebRequest/Invoke-RestMethod/iwr/irm invocation on its own command text (line continuations joined, up to the first |, ;, } or line end); each invocation in an allowlisted script must carry the required option.
F-T4-REVIEW-001.retest: web-request-rule-checks-every-invocation: the real ensure-omniroute.ps1 passes; with the first -MaximumRedirection 0 removed (the reviewer's reproduction) exactly one violation is reported; a mixed guarded/unguarded script fails, a line-continued guarded request passes, a guarded request outside the allowlist fails. Reverting to the file-wide check makes this scenario fail.

F-T4-REVIEW-002.observed: runPs and runNode collapsed every result other than exit 0 into false, so a spawn error, timeout or signal satisfied the negative (tamper rejected) assertions.
F-T4-REVIEW-002.fix: verdict() interprets a verifier result only after a real execution: a spawn error, a signal or a non-integer status fails the test; only an integer non-zero exit counts as rejection. Both verifiers must report the expected verdict.
F-T4-REVIEW-002.retest: verifier-results-require-a-real-execution: timeout (null status with ETIMEDOUT), signal, null status and spawn error all throw; exit 1 is REJECT and exit 0 is ACCEPT; the differential scenario uses the verdicts. Reverting verdict() to the collapsed form makes this scenario fail.

findings.summary: the web-request rule was a substring test over raw source: the text '-MaximumRedirection 0' anywhere in the invocation's text segment satisfied it, so 'Invoke-WebRequest "$u" -MaximumRedirection 01', 'Invoke-WebRequest "$u" # -MaximumRedirection 0' and 'Invoke-WebRequest "$u" -UserAgent "-MaximumRedirection 0"' all returned no violation although none disables redirects
findings.rootCause: compliance evidence was taken from raw source text, so comments and string contents counted as code, and the value was matched as a text prefix instead of as the parameter's parsed value
findings.fix: PARSE_CODE (the one PowerShell 5.1 parser path, detectPs1) now also returns, for every CommandAst in the file (nested script blocks included), the command name and its elements: parameter name, colon argument or the argument node's AST type, source text, string-constant value and quote kind. Comments never appear in this view, and string contents only appear as the value of their own argument. In the allowlisted script every parsed Invoke-WebRequest/Invoke-RestMethod/iwr/irm command must carry exactly one -MaximumRedirection parameter, written out in full, whose value (colon argument or following element) is a ConstantExpressionAst with source text exactly '0'. So 01, 00, 0x0, $x and quoted '0' are rejected. Every raw-text mention of a web-request name not matched by a parsed web-request command (comment, string) is a further violation, and outside the allowlist every mention is still a violation, as before. WEB_ALLOWED is now a set of file names.

findings.summary: the Set-ExecutionPolicy exemption regex accepted '-Scope Process' inside a trailing comment ('Set-ExecutionPolicy Unrestricted # -Scope Process'), and the entry-script regex accepted a commented-out '# $ErrorActionPreference="Stop"'
findings.rootCause: same family as F-T4-C1-001: exemption and requirement evidence were regex matches over raw source including comments and strings
findings.fix: a parsed Set-ExecutionPolicy command is persistent unless it carries exactly one real -Scope parameter whose value (colon argument or following element) is the string constant Process. Every raw-text mention of Set-ExecutionPolicy not matched by a parsed command (comment, or a string passed to a child shell) is a violation. Entry scripts (all except the sanitize-process-env.ps1 helper) need an AssignmentStatementAst whose left side is exactly $ErrorActionPreference, whose operator is '=', whose right side is the single- or double-quoted string constant Stop, and which is an unconditional top-level statement of the script (parent is a named block of the root script block). An assignment in a comment, a block comment, a string, a function body (a function-local variable never affects the script scope) or a conditional block does not count. The prohibited-text rules (EncodedCommand / -enc, DownloadString/DownloadFile, pipe to Invoke-Expression) deliberately still scan the raw source: comments and strings can only add violations there, and string scanning still catches code handed to a child shell, so no existing rule was weakened

advisoryCovered.note: the independent Claude pre-review found the EncodedCommand, DownloadString/DownloadFile, Set-ExecutionPolicy and $ErrorActionPreference rules had no positive control. The new regression scenario adds positive controls for each, plus pipe to Invoke-Expression, and the blind-* mutants below show each control fails when its rule is blinded

regressionScenario.name: safety-rules-credit-only-parsed-code-not-comments-or-strings
reported: F-T4-C1-001 repros: -MaximumRedirection 01; -MaximumRedirection 0 only in a comment; -MaximumRedirection 0 only inside -UserAgent's string
Stop assignment only in a block comment, only inside a string, only inside a function body
EncodedCommand parameter, -enc abbreviation, EncodedCommand inside a Start-Process argument string
regressionScenario.mechanics: fixtures are written to a fresh os.tmpdir() directory (one subdirectory each, so the allowlisted name ensure-omniroute.ps1 can repeat), parsed by the same detectPs1 as the real scripts (a fixture parse error fails the scenario), evaluated by the same safetyViolations, and removed afterwards. Every expected report and every unexpected report is collected and the scenario fails listing all of them. The existing web-request-rule-checks-every-invocation scenario keeps its five assertions and messages unchanged and now evaluates its in-memory sources through the same parser path. tests/pkg-t4-powershell-safety.test.ts pins PASS 7/7 (was 6/6) and requires PASS for powershell-scripts-follow-safety-rules and the new scenario by name, in addition to the two scenarios it already named

remediationRounds.realCorpus: all 13 scripts/*.ps1 remain compliant under the stricter rules with no script changes: the 12 entry scripts each have one unconditional top-level $ErrorActionPreference="Stop" (double-quoted), ensure-omniroute.ps1 has exactly two web-request mentions, both parsed Invoke-WebRequest commands with -MaximumRedirection 0 (ConstantExpressionAst, text '0'), and no script mentions Set-ExecutionPolicy, EncodedCommand or DownloadString/DownloadFile
